lead.question:
∀ {Ω : Type} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}, IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X →
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      (∑' k : ℕ, ℙ {ω | (maxLocalTime X (2 ^ k) ω : ℝ) /
        (Real.log ((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ 2 < 1 / π - ε}) ≠ ∞
lead.title: Erdős Problem 1166 — dembo peres rosen zeitouni · step 2

review.statement: For every probability space (Ω, ℙ), every X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ satisfying `IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X`, and every real ε > 0, the ℝ≥0∞ sum over k ∈ ℕ of ℙ{ω | maxLocalTime X (2^k) ω / (log(2^k))² < 1/π − ε} is finite. In the upstream definitions, the increments are measurable, mutually independent and uniform on the four lattice unit steps. The position starts at the origin, and local time counts visits at times 0 through n inclusive. [Walk definitions](https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/src/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/%C2%AB1165%C2%BB/) [Maximum local time](https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/src/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/%C2%AB1166%C2%BB/)
review.significance: The finite sum gives the almost-sure dyadic lower bound by Borel–Cantelli. Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni already established the quantitative lower-tail estimate behind this step in §5 of their 2001 paper. [Acta Mathematica paper](https://www.math.csi.cuny.edu/~rosen/64-erdos-taylor.pdf)
review.settlement_test: A bound on the stated probabilities by a summable sequence for all sufficiently large k settles the mathematical statement. The exact Lean target requires an independent kernel replay in the pinned queue environment, with declaration-type and axiom checks.
review.aliases: Erdős–Taylor conjecture on the planar random walk, maximum local time, and thick points of planar random walk. H2 is the dyadic lower-tail summability step of the Dembo–Peres–Rosen–Zeitouni variant. Erdős and Taylor posed the maximum-local-time conjecture in 1960. Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni proved it in 2001, and Jay Rosen gave a direct random-walk proof in 2005. [Erdős and Taylor](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-17.pdf) [1999 preprint](https://cims.nyu.edu/~zeitouni/pdf/dprzplanarsent.pdf) [2001 paper](https://www.math.csi.cuny.edu/~rosen/64-erdos-taylor.pdf) [Rosen](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503108)

review.proof_or_witness: Let c = 1/π − ε. For c ≤ 0 the event is empty because the normalized local time is nonnegative. Otherwise choose c < b < 1/π and α ∈ (0,1) with bα² > c. Put N = 2^k, j = ⌊αk⌋, m = 2^j and r = 2^(k−j). Since log m / log N = j/k → α, eventually b(log m)² > c(log N)². By Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni, Theorem 1.1, the probability that a canonical m-step walk has maximum local time at least b(log m)² tends to 1. Counting the visit at time zero as well changes the maximum by at most one. Thus the block success probability is at least 1/2 for large m. Divide the N increments into r disjoint blocks of m increments. Subtract each block's starting site. Each translated block maximum depends only on its own increments, so these maxima are mutually independent and have the canonical m-step law. Every block visit count, including both endpoints, is bounded by the full-walk count at the corresponding site. Full-walk failure therefore forces failure of all r blocks and has probability at most (1/2)^r. Because k−j ≥ (1−α)k, eventually r ≥ k. The resulting bound by (1/2)^k is summable. Each of the finitely many initial terms is at most one, including k = 0 where Lean real division gives zero. This is the block amplification used in §5 of the original proof. [Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni](https://www.math.csi.cuny.edu/~rosen/64-erdos-taylor.pdf)
review.remaining_obligation: The main missing Lean lemma under the same Ω, ℙ, X and `IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X` hypotheses is `∀ b : ℝ, 0 < b → b < 1 / π → ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop, (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ℙ {ω | b * (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤ (maxLocalTime X m ω : ℝ)}`. Formalize this probability estimate with credit to Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni, then formalize the measurable finite-block law, independence, and geometric comparison.
